note: ساحل means coast/shore/beachfront and is also used as the given name Sahil. The source's specific 'female given name' label is unreliable; Sahil is commonly masculine in South Asia.
بس is a major homograph/discourse word: bus; enough/that's enough; only/just; stop! It can also be a stem of بسنا in context. 'Stem' alone is not a learner meaning and adjective POS is not useful.
proposed_english: bus; enough; that's enough; only/just; stop!; dwell/settle (verb stem, context-dependent)

note: فائدہ centrally means benefit/advantage/usefulness/profit. The source's bare 'use' can be misleading as the verb 'use'.
ہاں is the affirmative particle/interjection 'yes'. Noun POS is incorrect.
خدا means God/Lord/deity. 'Husband' is confusion with خداوند or an archaic compound sense and should not be taught as a direct meaning of خدا.
حملے is an inflected form of حملہ and must explicitly give attack/attacks rather than only inflection labels.
دورہ is a noun meaning visit/tour/round and, in medical contexts, attack/fit. 'Content word' is not a POS.
جسے is an oblique/dative relative pronoun meaning whom/which/to whom or which. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
proposed_english: whom; which; to whom; to which

note: واقع in this high-frequency use means located/situated and functions as an adjective/participle, not a verb. It can also mean occurring/actual in related contexts.
عالم is a vocalization-dependent homograph: عالَم means world/realm, while عالِم means scholar/learned person. 'Wise; doctor' is imprecise and misses 'scholar'.
proposed_english: world; realm; scholar; learned person (depending on vocalization/context)

note: عورت centrally means woman and can mean wife contextually. 'Pudendum' is contamination from a related Arabic lexical item and should not appear as a standard Urdu meaning.
دوسرا means second/other/another. The transliteration-like gloss 'doosra' is not an English meaning and should be removed.
فٹ is both the English-derived unit 'foot/feet' and the common loan adjective 'fit' in Urdu. The latter homograph is omitted.
proposed_english: foot/feet (unit of measure); fit; fitted (loanword, context-dependent)

note: ہمارا means our/ours (masculine singular), not my/mine. The current first-person singular definition is a serious pronoun error.
